claim: Theorem 7 of Sahu, Chaudhary, and Gupta (2026) is false under its stated hypotheses. Let \(X\sim\operatorname{Uniform}(0,1)\), let \(Y=X+2\sim\operatorname{Uniform}(2,3)\), and take the common weight \(w_1=w_2=w\) with \(w(x)=e^{-x}\). Then \(w\) is positive, integrable on both supports, and strictly decreasing; also \(X\leq_{\mathrm{disp}}Y\) because every corresponding interquantile range is equal. For the paper's weighted cumulative residual quantile extropy, \(Q_X(p)=p\), \(Q_Y(p)=p+2\), and \(q_X(p)=q_Y(p)=1\), so for every \(0<u<1\), \(\Phi_{Q_Y}^{w}(u)=e^{-2}\Phi_{Q_X}^{w}(u)\). Since \(\Phi_{Q_X}^{w}(u)<0\), this gives \(\Phi_{Q_X}^{w}(u)<\Phi_{Q_Y}^{w}(u)\), the strict reverse of Theorem 7's conclusion. The obstruction is structural: dispersive order is invariant under translations, whereas a value-dependent decreasing weight need not be. The proof's step from dispersive order to the opposite usual stochastic order requires an additional location/support condition that is absent from the theorem statement.
integrity: The theorem statement, its defining integral, and the proof step invoking usual stochastic order were read in the open-access primary source. The counterexample was reconstructed symbolically from the stated definition. A closely related earlier full-text paper was inspected to check how endpoint hypotheses enter the dispersive-to-stochastic comparison. No independent external audit has been performed.
scientific_limitations: The result refutes Theorem 7 under its printed hypotheses and identifies a missing location/support restriction. It does not claim a maximal corrected theorem, and it does not rule out a later corrigendum or nonindexed independent observation of the same issue.
title: Translation breaks a dispersive-order theorem for weighted cumulative residual quantile extropy
